title: From protocol identifiers to behaviour
dominant: Port labels and content signatures provided direct signals. The early corpus then moves to host behaviour and flow statistics.
change: BLINC uses transport-level interactions; Bayesian classification learns statistical discriminators; early identification asks how soon a flow can be recognised.
unresolved: Encryption, dynamic ports and changing applications weaken direct identifiers. Early decisions must also account for unknown traffic.
sourceType: Original paper; synthesis across linked papers

title: Learn the representation, retain the context
dominant: Classical statistics remained useful while neural models began learning from packet bytes, packet-length sequences and multimodal flow inputs.
change: AppScanner targets encrypted mobile apps. Deep Packet, FS-Net, MIMETIC and DISTILLER explore different input units and combinations; DeepMAL extends byte learning to malware traffic.
unresolved: A better network architecture cannot repair ambiguous labels, capture-specific features or incompatible preprocessing. The traffic unit becomes a central experimental choice.
sourceType: Original paper; synthesis across linked papers

title: Pretraining becomes a research programme
dominant: PERT and ET-BERT adapt learned tokenisation and masked objectives. YaTC and Flow-MAE reconstruct masked traffic representations; contrastive approaches investigate limited labels.
change: The question expands from training a classifier to learning a reusable representation. Packet, burst and flow boundaries encode different assumptions. Trustee adds a parallel route: explain a model’s decisions to diagnose shortcut learning.
unresolved: Multiple datasets with separate supervised fine-tuning do not establish cross-network transfer. Rosetta and the FlowPic replication show why changes in traces and data collection matter.
sourceType: Original paper; synthesis across linked papers

title: Move from model latency to operational cost
dominant: Deployment research treats measurement, feature extraction, observation delay and inference as one pipeline.
change: Traffic Refinery quantifies representation costs; ServeFlow uses a fast path and a slower path. IIsy, BoS, Leo and P4 studies investigate constrained hardware; CATO optimises the pipeline.
unresolved: A GPU samples-per-second result does not predict line-rate operation. Queueing, minority errors and confidence-based escalation require workload-specific evaluation.
sourceType: Original paper; synthesis across linked papers

title: Efficiency advances; evidence standards tighten
dominant: State-space models, graph representations, protocol-aware tokenisation and foundation-style pretraining coexist with systematic critiques.
change: Alongside more efficient representations, NTC Enigma probes ET-BERT and YaTC with controlled occlusions. BiasSeeker ranks suspicious fields for expert review; ShortcutCatcher uses verification-set feedback to remove shortcut features.
unresolved: Diagnosis, mitigation and deployment robustness require different evidence. Within-dataset occlusions and forged network shifts leave independently collected cross-organisation tests open. Representative labelled verification data, unknown classes, calibration and serving cost remain important questions.
sourceType: Original paper; synthesis across linked papers
